newsitem.title: UK: ASDA off on downgrade, bond redemption.
newsitem.headline: ASDA off on downgrade, bond redemption.

text.p: Shares in supermarket operator ASDA Group Plc fell on Wednesday after the retailer announced a bond redemption and analysts at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett cut the stock to "hold" from "undervalued," dealers said.
The stock was down 1-3/4p or, 1.41 percent, at 122p by 1216 GMT.
ASDA said it would redeem all its 10-3/4 percent convertible capital bonds due 2005 on February 7. Dealers said the announcement had hit the share price.
"The story on the bonds redemption seems to be behind the move today," one market-maker said.

"Some people might be worried that a technical situation exists which might result in an overhang of stock, although it won't be a big problem." Another market-maker said the bond redemption had "dampened sentiment" in the stock.
At Hoare Govett analysts were not immediately available for comment.
Dealers added that UK retail shares had been weak in recent days due to fears of a near-term domestic interest rate rise, which could choke off the recent recovery in consumer spending.
"It's not just Hoare Govett which has gone more cautious on ASDA, I think a few other houses are moving that way on the retailers," one market source said.

Other retailing stocks had a mixed morning. Argos Plc was down half a penny at 730-1/2 after a 20p fall on Tuesday, but Great Universal Stores Plc and Marks and Spencer Plc both recovered some of Tuesday's losses.
Marks and Spencer was up 4-1/2p at 484-1/2 while GUS rose half a penny at 615-1/2.
